_help: Per commodity, an indicator->1-5 map (5 = bullish). A bare number or {"score": n, "note": "why"} for auditability. Unset = held at neutral and excluded from the average, exactly like fundamentals_manual. Refreshed by the fx-strength-desk-daily task, step 2c.

Real yield direction.note: 7 Oct: 10-year ended at 5.295%, a new cycle high, and the Fed minutes showed most officials see another hike by year end. Headwind intact, held at 1.

US dollar direction.note: 7 Oct: DXY +0.4% to 102.25 with yields; gold closed at a two-month low ($4,110). Waller's 'hikes need not be consecutive' gave only brief relief on 8 Oct. Held at 1.5.

Central-bank & ETF demand.note: WGC (early Oct): gold ETFs took in $10bn in September even as gold fell 8.5%, capping a record $31bn Q3 with holdings at a record 4,256t; CB buying still record pace. ETF leg turned supportive again, 4 -> 4.5.

Safe-haven bid.note: Hormuz tanker attacks hit their highest weekly level of the war and the US reportedly drew up Iran strike options (7-8 Oct), yet gold fell to a two-month low - the haven bid is being overpowered by yields. Cut 3 -> 2.5.

Real yield direction.note: 7 Oct: 10-year ended at 5.295%, a new cycle high, and the Fed minutes showed most officials see another hike by year end. Headwind intact, held at 1. Silver more leveraged to it.

US dollar direction.note: 7 Oct: DXY +0.4% to 102.25 with yields; gold closed at a two-month low ($4,110). Waller's 'hikes need not be consecutive' gave only brief relief on 8 Oct. Held at 1.5.

Industrial demand.note: Re-checked 9 Oct: no newer data - solar silver use still falling (thrifting/copper substitution, PV demand -7% to -19% in 2026), partly offset by data centres/autos; sixth straight deficit (~46 Moz). Held at 2.5.

Gold-silver ratio.note: Ratio ~70.2 (XAU 4149 / XAG 59.1 on the 8 Oct feed), up from ~67.9 as silver underperforms, but still below the long-run ~80. Neutral, held at 3.

OPEC+ supply policy.note: OPEC+ core seven held November quotas at the September level (31.1 Mb/d) on 4 Oct, extending the pause through year-end; next meeting 1 Nov. Restraint intact, held at 4.

Inventory trend.note: EIA week to 2 Oct: crude -3.2 Mb vs a 1.7 Mb build expected (424.1 Mb, ~1% above 5-yr), gasoline +0.4 Mb, distillates flat at 12% below 5-yr; Storm Isaias shut ~25% of Gulf output. Turned mildly bullish, 2.5 -> 3.5.

Demand outlook.note: EIA October STEO (6 Oct): 2026 demand -1.7 mb/d y/y, IEA last at -2.5 mb/d (next report 14 Oct), only OPEC sees growth (+0.4). EIA raised its Q4 Brent call to $105 on supply, not demand. Held at 1.5.

Geopolitical risk premium.note: Hormuz tanker attacks at their highest weekly level since the war began, a tanker hit north of Qatar (7 Oct) and reports of Pentagon strike options; Oman-Iran talks 'advanced' but confidence eroding. WTI +3% to ~$91. 3 -> 3.5.
